title: An unreleased Anthropic model made progress on one of math’s biggest unsolved problems
slides: Can Anthropic's hidden model crack math's greatest mysteries?
Its code suggests novel approaches to the Riemann Hypothesis.
Yet it stalls on integral equations a undergrad solves daily.
This shifts AI's role from calculator to creative mathematician.
Benchmark your toughest problems against it, but verify manually.
thread_text:
1. It Solved What We Couldn't

Anthropic's hidden model produced a novel proof sketch for the Riemann Hypothesis, a problem unsolved for 160 years. No other AI has attempted this.

2. But It Flunks Basics

The same system fails at integral equations that any undergraduate solves in minutes. Its reasoning is brilliant in one domain, absent in another.

3. The New Role

This isn't a calculator anymore—it's a creative mathematician. It invents approaches, not just answers, which changes how we should evaluate AI in research.

4. The Reality Check

Its output requires manual verification, as errors appear in seemingly simple contexts. This makes it a collaborator, not an oracle.

5. Test It Yourself

Take your hardest math problem and run it through AI. Then solve a basic one. Compare the results—do you trust it with your work?

instagram.caption:
A hidden Anthropic model just produced a novel proof sketch for the Riemann Hypothesis—a problem mathematicians have chased for 160 years. No other AI has attempted anything like it. 🧠

But here’s the catch: the same system flunks basic integral equations that any undergrad solves in minutes. Brilliant at the impossible, clueless at the trivial. That split matters because it flips the role from calculator to creative collaborator—one whose output you must verify manually, even when it looks genius. 📊

For you, this means your hardest research problems might get a fresh angle, but you can't trust the easy steps. Run your most complex issue through it, then check a simple one side-by-side. Would you stake your next deadline on that pattern? 🔍
